title: Whole Numbers: Place Value, Ordering and Large Numbers
seo_title: Whole Numbers and Place Value – JSS 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Count, read and write whole numbers up to trillions; give the place value of digits; compare and order numbers; use large numbers in everyday life. (summary of the NERDC JSS 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free JSS 1 maths worksheets on whole numbers: place value up to billions, the value of a digit, ×10 and ÷10, ordering numbers and inequality signs. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Each place is ten times the place to its right: units, tens, hundreds, thousands, …, millions, billions.
  • The value of a digit is the digit × its place value.
  • Multiplying by 10 moves every digit one place to the left; dividing by 10 moves every digit one place to the right.

Examples

Example

Value of 6 in 3,462,018

6 is in the ten thousands place

Answer: 60,000

Example

4.7 × 1,000

Digits move 3 places left

Answer: 4,700

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding a zero to multiply decimals by 104.7 × 10 = 47, not 4.70.
Comparing from the rightCompare from the highest place.
Confusing million and billion1 billion = 1,000 million.

items.q: Which statement is true?
